title: ZeroSOC source profile
description: What one security technology's records mean in the framework's terms: where each required input of Detection & Analysis §1.1 lives, what the source's own words mean, where every field of its record lands on the Case, and which of the framework's questions it can answer. It changes when the framework changes. How to talk to the technology — authentication, endpoints, paging, query language, permissions — is not here: that changes when the vendor's API does and lives with the integration.

id.description: The identifier a capability binding names this profile by.

product.description: The product name, as the Case's provenance records it.

api.description: The API and version these paths are read from.

profile_version.description: The date this profile was last true of the source.

override.description: Written by the loader, never by hand: present when the deployment read this profile through a local override (the binding's source_profile_overrides), and what the run records about it. A profile that ships carries none.

file.description: The override's file name, beside the binding.

sha256.description: The digest of the override file as it was read.

reason.description: Why the deployment overrides the shipped profile, in its own words.

base_profile_version.description: The profile_version of the shipped profile the override was written against.

stale.description: The shipped profile has moved past that version: the fix the override stands in for may have landed.

paths.description: What the override sets, as paths of this profile.

fields.description: Where each thing the framework needs lives on a record of this source. A path is dotted; [] steps into a list.

telemetry_rows.description: Where a row of this source's telemetry belongs in OCSF, for the evidence a Finding rests on. A column this table does not name is kept under its own name rather than dropped, so a mapping that lags the source loses nothing.

objects.description: column -> the path of the OCSF object attribute it fills, as a list of steps.

times.description: The columns a row states its time in, tried in turn.

uids.description: What this source calls a row's own identifier.

process_lineage.description: What this source calls the columns a process lineage is rebuilt from, on a row of its process telemetry: the name the lineage script uses (device, pid, created, name, command_line, parent_pid, parent_created, parent_name, parent_command_line, parent_parent_pid, parent_parent_created) -> the source's column. It is apart from `objects` because the identity of a process is its device, its id and its creation time together, read as the source writes them, and not an attribute placed on an OCSF object.

vocabularies.description: The source's own words, in the framework's and OCSF's terms. A word absent from a vocabulary is recorded as the source said it and never guessed at.

determination.description: The source's own account of WHAT the activity was, beside its verdict. Each word names the verdicts it may accompany, so an executor closing a Case in the source proposes only the words that verdict admits; `only` marks a verdict that admits one word, which is not a choice to make. A source with no such axis declares nothing here.

verdict_ids.description: The framework verdicts this word may be written with.

name.description: The word as the source's own interface shows it.

only.description: This is the one word those verdicts admit: it is written without asking.

analytic_types.description: Detection source -> the OCSF analytic type it is. One not listed is Other (99).

remediation_states.description: What the source says it did to an entity. One not listed is recorded as reported and never treated as neutralized.

neutralized.description: Whether the entity was taken out of play.

activity.description: OCSF Remediation Activity: Isolate, Evict, Restore. Null where the source did nothing to the entity.

tactics.description: The source's category -> the ATT&CK tactic it names. A category not listed names no tactic.

case_map.description: Every path of the source's record: where it lands on the Case, or why nothing reads it. This is the block that makes silence impossible — a field the vendor adds tomorrow is neither mapped nor ignored, and the completeness test fails.

path.description: Dotted path on the source's record; [] steps into a list.

case.description: Where it lands on the Case, as a dotted path of the Case Schema ([] steps into a list; the source's own object as unmapped.<extension key>; an attribute of the OCSF class the Case Schema does not state is addressed as OCSF names it). A list where one path of the source lands in more than one place.

ignored.description: Why nothing reads it. A reason, never a blank.

extension.description: The object this source keeps on the Case, under unmapped, for what it states and neither OCSF nor the framework carries.

key.description: The key of this source's object under the Case's unmapped: the source's own identifier.

capability_coverage.description: What of the framework's questions this source answers, and how well.

capabilities.description: capability class -> what this source answers of it.

answers.description: The question it answers, in the method's terms.

limits.description: What it does not answer, or answers partly: the licence tier, the retention window, the field that is null.

operation.description: The integration's operation, where one name is stable enough to record.

data_sources.description: required_data_sources name, exactly as a playbook writes it -> whether this source can answer it, with the query recipe or the alerts that do. What the source can answer is not what a deployment has: a licence tier without the telemetry tables answers none of the recipes, and it is the deployment's binding that says so.

queries.description: Per question kind, the recipe that asks it of this tool.

asks.description: The question, in the method's terms.

recipe.description: The query, in the tool's own language, with the entity as a parameter.

paths.description: name the framework uses -> path on the source's record.

id_map.description: The source's word -> the framework's id and name.

type.description: An object is the source's own key-value pairs, kept whole; an array declares its items.

from.description: The path on the source's record it is read from.

items.description: What each item of an array is: a value of a scalar type, or an object whose properties are declared as these are.
